```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(SegreCP)
```

## One iteration

A fit with CP rank `r` keeps `r` rank-one components. One iteration updates
each component once, in turn, with the other components at their current
values, so each update already uses the components updated before it in the
same iteration.

* RGD projects the gradient of the objective onto the tangent space of the
  Segre manifold at the component and takes a step of size `step_size`.
* RGN minimizes the objective over the tangent space at the component. In
  decomposition this is RGD with step size 1. In regression it solves the
  least-squares problem in the tangent coordinates.

Every update is retracted to a rank-one tensor by the rank-(1, ..., 1)
T-HOSVD, computed exactly from one 2 x 2 eigenproblem per mode.

## Two profiles

`segre_control()` has two profiles. The `"manuscript"` profile (the default)
runs the algorithms analyzed in the paper: the components are updated in the
order 1, ..., r, RGD uses a fixed step, and all `max_iter` iterations are run.
The default step sizes, 0.5 for decomposition and \(\sigma_X^{-2}\)
(`1 / design_variance`) for regression, are those covered by the convergence
results of the paper.

```{r}
segre_control(max_iter = 20)
```

The `"practical"` profile updates the components in decreasing order of their
weights, stops when the relative decrease of the objective is at most
`1e-6`, and uses backtracking for regression RGD. Each option can also be set
directly.

```{r}
segre_control(profile = "practical", max_iter = 200)
```

## Starts

CPCA and HOSVD are spectral starts. For an orthogonal CP tensor both recover
the components.

```{r}
dims <- c(3, 4, 5)
factors <- lapply(dims, function(p) diag(p)[, 1:2, drop = FALSE])
truth <- cp_components(c(3, 1.5), factors)
x <- reconstruct_cp(truth)

init_cpca <- cp_initialize(x, rank = 2, method = "cpca", split = 1)
init_hosvd <- cp_initialize(x, rank = 2, method = "hosvd")

cp_relative_error(init_cpca$comps, truth)
cp_relative_error(init_hosvd$comps, truth)
```

A start can also be a list of components, or a function of the tensor and
the rank that returns one. Further arguments of the function are passed in
`init_args`.

```{r}
perturbed_start <- function(x, rank, scale) {
  cp_components(scale * c(3, 1.5), factors)
}
fit <- segre_decompose(
  x, rank = 2, method = "rgn",
  init = perturbed_start, init_args = list(scale = 0.9),
  control = segre_control(max_iter = 2)
)
fit
```
